MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFE’S MOTION FOR LEAVE
TO FILE A SUPPLEMENTAL MEMORANDUM ADDRESSING ECF NO. 74

Plaintiff seeks leave to file one supplemental memorandum in support of his pending Rule
26(d)(1) motion. ECF No. 15. The ground is a filing Defendants made after the discovery briefing
closed. Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) requires leave for further briefs. This memorandum states why
leave should be granted.

I. NCMEC’s September 18 Filing Renews the Premise of the Pending Discovery

Motion.

The sequence is short. Plaintiff filed ECF No. 15 on August 20, 2026, requesting leave to
serve three source-identification interrogatories before the Rule 26(f) conference. Plaintiff filed a
sworn declaration stating his account-naming history. ECF No. 31. Plaintiff then moved for leave

to file a Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint containing corresponding source-

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 79 Filed 09/18/26 Page 2 of 4 PagelD# 794

identification allegations. ECF Nos. 59-60. On September 18, 2026, Defendants Katie Hall and
NCMEC opposed that motion. ECF No. 74.

ECF No. 74 renews two propositions. It describes the statements at issue as concerning
reports received “for any of the three identifiers in Plaintiff’s subpoena to NCMEC.” ECF No. 74 at
5. It states that Plaintiff “cannot plausibly assert falsity, because he does not have access to those
reports,” and that “[n]o allegations Plaintiff can make can change that fact.” Id. ECF No. 74 applies
those propositions to the proposed source-identification allegations. ECF No. 74 at 4-6.

ECF No. 74 is not one more filing that mentions the reports. ECF No. 74 renews the
position that the reports’ asserted contents defeat Plaintiff’s claims while Plaintiff’s inability to
inspect the reports defeats any challenge. That is the premise the three interrogatories were drafted
to test. The renewal came after the discovery briefing closed. The renewal is the ground for
supplementation.

Il. The Supplement Addresses the Decision Before the Court.

Two decisions are distinct. The first is whether this subsequent development may be added
to the briefing on ECF No. 15. The second is whether the requested discovery should be authorized.
This motion presents only the first. Exhibit A addresses the second, and the Court will resolve it in
ruling on ECF No. 15.

The supplement’s contribution is specific. It places NCMEC’s September 18 formulations
beside the exact questions already proposed. It explains why the three answers address NCMEC’s
own asserted premise. The Court deciding ECF No. 15 should have that development before it.

II. The Supplement Permits Focused Adjudication Without Expanding

Discovery.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 79 Filed 09/18/26 Page 3 of 4 PagelD# 795

Exhibit A has one confined subject: ECF No. 74’s renewed truth and lack-of-access
arguments. Exhibit A relies on docket materials only: ECF Nos. 11, 15-1, 31, and 74. Exhibit A
attaches no new declaration. Exhibit A changes no interrogatory, no exclusion, and no permitted
answer. The substantive discovery argument appears in Exhibit A, not here.

Plaintiff requests leave to file Exhibit A and its consideration with ECF No. 15. Any

responsive submission is for the Court’s direction. Leave should be granted.
